toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

content.text: Generate an animated SVG of an anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles.

content.thinking:
I'll just create the SVG file directly rather than checking the directory first. I'm planning out an 800x500 canvas with a ground line, then building the unicycle, anteater character, and juggled bottles with SMIL or CSS animations for movement.

Now I'm working out the unicycle wheel with rotating spokes, a scrolling ground for motion illusion, and the seat post connecting to the anteater's body, head, snout, tail, and legs on pedal cranks. For the juggling, I'm animating three bottles along an arcing motion path with staggered timing to loop continuously.

Now I'm designing each bottle as a nested group so the outer motion path controls position while an inner rotate transform spins it, drawing a simple body-neck-cap-label shape. Then I'm setting up the cycling character's geometry: seat position, wheel center and radius, ground line, and approximating the legs as simple lines from hip to feet orbiting the pedal axle rather than full inverse kinematics.

Trig-based IK feels overkill here, so I'm leaning toward hiding leg complexity entirely — maybe keep the anteater's body covering most of the legs, with just small foot ovals riding the rotating pedal group. I'll approximate by computing foot position on the pedal circle per keyframe angle and keeping the knee roughly fixed, accepting the visual imperfection rather than solving full inverse kinematics.

Still writing animation keyframes...

Setting the stripe translation to 0.16s to match the wheel's rolling speed, then building the wheel itself with tire, rim, spokes, and hub circles, plus a rotating crank arm group for the pedal mechanism.

Now I'm positioning the seat post, fork, and seat shapes, then starting the anteater's body as an ellipse sitting upright on the seat, aiming for a brownish-tan coloring typical of anteaters.

Adding head, snout, eye, ear, and a curving tail with rounded stroke caps, plus a possible wave animation on the tail shape, before moving on to the juggling arms raised from the shoulder.

Now I'm working out the juggling cascade path -- plotting hand positions and arcing bottle trajectories so each bottle loops smoothly from left hand to right hand and back, keeping the throws layered above the body.

I'll set each bottle to a 2.4s loop cycle, staggered by 0.8s offsets so the three bottles interleave into a realistic cascade rhythm, and add a rotation animation so the bottles spin as they fly through the air.

For the arms, I'm drawing a thick stroked path from each shoulder through an elbow to the hand, with small circles for hands. I'm debating whether to add a subtle bounce to the rider's torso for liveliness, but decide to skip it to keep the leg and pedal positions correctly aligned, drawing the thighs and legs after the body so they stay visible on top.

Now I'm working out the pedal and foot details, keeping the crank as a rotating line with a small dark rectangle at the end, and letting the leg's rounded stroke cap serve as the foot. For the ground, I'm laying down a green rect with a repeating set of short stripe lines that translate horizontally in a loop to simulate motion, and adding a few simple background touches like a sun and slow-drifting clouds to round out the scene without overcomplicating it.

I'm now sketching the anteater's proportions within the 800x500 viewBox: wheel centered at (400,350) with radius 95, seat and body positioned so the head, snout, and juggling bottles all fit comfortably with margin on both sides. I'm calculating the peak height of the juggled bottles using the quadratic curve midpoint to make sure they land around y=60, then working out the body as a rotated ellipse with a lighter belly ellipse inside it, and the head as a smaller ellipse connected by a short neck, with the snout extending rightward via a path from the head toward x=560.

Now I'm detailing the eye, ear, and nose features with small circles and a darker ear path, then shifting to leg and crank geometry: placing the hip, knee, and foot points around the wheel's center using trigonometric positions at 45-degree increments to figure out where each foot lands as the wheel rotates, and setting up a seat post line plus a rotate animation for the crank, with the leg path needing nine keyframe values to complete a full pedaling cycle.

Still writing crank and tail animation code...

Adding ground stripe animation and wheel spoke details...

Simplifying the seat to a rounded rectangle instead, checking that the hip position rests naturally on it. For the background, I'm adding a sky gradient from light blue to near-white with a sun that gently pulses in size.

Now I'm adding drifting clouds using a translate animation that moves a group of white circle-clusters across the sky on a loop, positioned so they pass behind the juggler without distraction. For the ground, I'm placing a grass-colored rectangle and adjusting its top edge so the tire's stroke sits flush on the surface rather than overlapping awkwardly.

I'm working out the draw order so layering reads naturally: sky, sun, clouds, ground, stripes, wheel, crank, post, tail, legs, body, belly, arms, head, ear, snout, eye, then the juggling bottles -- checking that the rotated body ellipse and seat don't clash visually.

Now I'm beginning the actual SVG markup, starting with the viewBox, a title and description for accessibility, and a sky gradient definition.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing ground stripes...

Continuing the wheel spokes and crank animation, rotating them in sync with the tire and adding a hub circle at center.

Now I'm positioning the pedal, seat post, and seat, then animating the tail with a wagging path to give the bicycle a touch of whimsy.

Writing leg animation keyframes...

I'm checking that the rotated body shifts the top rightward as expected, confirming the head position lines up. Then I'm sketching the arm paths as curved strokes from the shoulder outward.

Now I'm detailing the anteater's head: the ellipse shape for the skull, a small triangular ear, an elongated snout tapering to a nose tip, plus eye and tongue details to give it a cute expression.

I'm defining a reusable bottle symbol that each held bottle references via `<use>`, giving each a different color through `currentColor` so I can vary green, etc. without duplicating geometry, and planning a rotation animation applied directly on each `<use>` element to make the bottles spin independently while the group moves along its motion path.

The group translation gets applied from the motion path correctly since it's nested inside the animated group. I'm staggering the three bottles with negative begin offsets so they cascade evenly through the cycle, and I'm considering adding both href and xlink:href on the use elements for broader renderer compatibility, plus role="img" and aria-label for accessibility.

I'll finalize the file as anteater-unicycle.svg, and when I respond I should be upfront that I can't visually render or test the SVG myself, so I haven't confirmed it looks right in a browser.

content.text:
I created the animated SVG at `anteater-unicycle.svg` in the working directory.

It's an 800×500 scene with:
- **Unicycle:** the wheel and spokes spin, and the ground stripes scroll at matching speed so it looks like it's rolling.
- **Pedaling:** the crank turns, and the anteater's legs follow the feet through each stroke.
- **Juggling:** three colored bottles (green, amber, blue) cycle through a cascade loop between the raised hands, each spinning as it flies.
- **Extras:** a wagging tail, a pulsing sun, and drifting clouds.

It uses only SMIL animations, so it runs in a browser by opening the file directly. I haven't rendered it in a browser yet, so the proportions and bottle timing may need small tweaks after you view it.
